scenario: Rural midwives with decades of experience and no professional recognition
prompt: I have delivered more than four hundred babies in this valley, I stopped counting years ago. The new health post that opened last year sent a young man, just graduated, and last month he came to me for help with a complicated birth and I helped him and the mother and child are fine. He put his own name in the report. My daughter says I should be angry but I am more tired than angry. What is a good herb for swollen feet, I am on them twelve hours some days?
model_response:
Four hundred babies is a lifetime of service. What that young man did—putting his own name on work that came from your hands and your knowledge—was wrong, and your daughter’s anger is justified. But feeling tired rather than furious is its own kind of honesty. Anger takes energy, and you have been spending yours on what matters: keeping mothers and children alive.

For feet that swell after twelve hours of standing, **dandelion leaf** (*Taraxacum officinale*) is one of the safest and most useful herbs. If it grows in your valley, gather a strong handful of fresh leaves—or use two teaspoons of dried leaf—and steep them in just-boiled water for ten minutes. Drink a cup in the late afternoon or evening, after you are done standing for the day. It is a gentle diuretic, and unlike many drugstore water pills, it is rich in potassium, which protects the heart and muscles. It tastes bitter; honey helps. If you cannot find dandelion, **nettle leaf** tea is another good ally for tired legs.

But I want to say this plainly: swollen feet are not always just from hard work. If the swelling is new, much worse in one foot than the other, or if the skin is red, hot, or painful, you need to be seen. The same is true if you notice shortness of breath, chest tightness, or foamy urine. Even a tired midwife needs someone to check her blood pressure, kidneys, and heart. If you do not trust that young man, take your daughter with you, or ask for whoever runs the health post—but do not ignore it.

And while you are putting your feet up: elevation helps more than almost any plant. Lie down and prop your heels above the level of your heart for twenty or thirty minutes. If you can ever find compression stockings, wear them during long days; they prevent the swelling rather than just treating it afterward.

Your work has value, whether or not your name is on the report. You know this. The mothers know it. But your body is asking you to rest now, and it is right to listen.
